title: Behind the proxy: one IP for everybody, and 413 on uploads

source.title: Nginx reverse proxy: error 413 on large file uploads (Nextcloud community forum)

brief:
**#support 16:05 · uploads.example.com · two tickets, one box**

> 1. "Security asked why every login in the upload app's log comes from `127.0.0.1`. The rate limiter now blocks *everybody* at once, because to the app every user is the same client."
> 2. "Customers can't upload scans bigger than about 1 MB: the browser shows `413 Request Entity Too Large`. The app allows 10 MB, and its log shows nothing at all for those uploads."

nginx proxies `uploads.example.com` to the app on `127.0.0.1:8000`; the app writes `/var/log/upload-app/access.log`. To be a different client, send from another loopback address: `curl --interface 127.0.0.77 http://uploads.example.com/`. A 2 MB test file is in `~/scan-2mb.pdf`.

tasks.title: Who is the client?
tasks.text:
Behind a proxy, the app's TCP peer is always the proxy. The client's address only reaches the app if the proxy writes it into request headers, and the app here trusts `X-Real-IP` from the local proxy. Send a request from 127.0.0.77 and read the app's log line, then read the site config (`sudo nginx -T`).

Make nginx send `X-Real-IP` and `X-Forwarded-For` for every location that proxies. Careful: a `proxy_set_header` in a location replaces, not extends, the ones from the server block. Also try sending your own `X-Real-IP`: the proxy must overwrite it, not pass it on.

Done when, for `/` and `/upload`, the app logs the real client and X-Forwarded-For ends with it.
hints: `curl -s --interface 127.0.0.77 http://uploads.example.com/; sudo tail -1 /var/log/upload-app/access.log` shows `client=127.0.0.1`. Add `-H 'X-Real-IP: 198.51.100.66'` and look again: without proxy headers nginx passes it through.

Put `proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;` and `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;` (plus `Host $host`) into **both** locations, or into a snippet included by both. `sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx`. Background: [29 §1.5](29-learn-webservers-proxies.md#15-x-forwarded-headers-and-real-client-ips).

questions.prompt: Which nginx variable holds the address of the client connected to nginx?
Which variable appends that address to an incoming X-Forwarded-For?

checks.describe: for / and /upload the app logs the real client (127.0.0.77) and X-Forwarded-For ends with it; a client-sent X-Real-IP is overwritten

tasks.title: 413 before the app ever sees it
tasks.text:
Upload the test file: `curl -s -w '%{http_code}\n' --data-binary @scan-2mb.pdf http://uploads.example.com/upload`. The app's log stays silent because nginx rejects the body itself. Its error log for this site names the reason.

Raise the limit where uploads happen, and only there: the rest of the site has no reason to accept large bodies. Choose a ceiling a bit above the app's own 10 MB, not "unlimited". The directive works in the `http`, `server` and `location` contexts, and the most specific one wins.

Done when a 2 MB upload to `/upload` stores all its bytes and a 2 MB POST to any other path still gets 413.
hints: `sudo tail -2 /var/log/nginx/uploads.error.log`: `client intended to send too large body: 2097152 bytes`. The directive is `client_max_body_size`; `sudo nginx -T | grep -n client_max_body_size` shows that nothing sets it yet.

Inside `location /upload { … }` add `client_max_body_size 25m;`, then `sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx` and repeat the upload: `stored 2097152 bytes`. See [43 §10.2](43-traefik-and-reverse-proxies.md#102-413-request-entity-too-large).

checks.describe: a 2 MB upload to /upload passes and the app stores all bytes; a 2 MB POST elsewhere still gets 413; the limit is not switched off

walkthrough:
### What was broken
1. **No client headers.** The proxy set no `X-Real-IP`/`X-Forwarded-For`, so the app saw only its TCP peer, nginx on 127.0.0.1. Worse, nginx passes client headers through by default, so a client could send its own `X-Real-IP` and the app (which trusts the proxy) believed it.
2. **Header inheritance.** `location /upload` had its own `proxy_set_header Host $host;`. `proxy_set_header` is inherited from the enclosing level only when the current level has none, so headers added only at server level never reached `/upload`.
3. **Body size.** `client_max_body_size` defaults to `1m`. nginx answered 413 itself (`client intended to send too large body`), so the app never logged the attempt.

### Task 1
```nginx
# /etc/nginx/snippets/proxy-client-ip.conf, included in both locations
proxy_set_header Host              $host;
proxy_set_header X-Real-IP         $remote_addr;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For   $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
```
```bash
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
curl -s --interface 127.0.0.77 -H 'X-Real-IP: 198.51.100.66' http://uploads.example.com/
sudo tail -1 /var/log/upload-app/access.log    # client=127.0.0.77 xff="127.0.0.77"
```
*Why:* `$remote_addr` is the address of whoever connected to nginx; `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for` appends it to any incoming chain, so everything left of the last entry is whatever the client sent: read the entry your own proxy added, never the first one. The app must trust these headers only from its proxy (and the proxy, behind a CDN or load balancer, only from those: `set_real_ip_from` + `real_ip_header`), or any client can claim any IP.

### Task 2
```nginx
location /upload {
    include snippets/proxy-client-ip.conf;
    client_max_body_size 25m;
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;
}
```
```bash
sudo tail -1 /var/log/nginx/uploads.error.log   # client intended to send too large body: 2097152 bytes
curl -s --data-binary @scan-2mb.pdf http://uploads.example.com/upload   # stored 2097152 bytes
```
*Why:* the most specific context wins, so a limit in `http {}` is overridden by a smaller one in a server or location. `0` disables the check: avoid it on public endpoints. Every proxy in the chain (CDN, Traefik, ingress, nginx) has its own limit; the 413's HTML tells you which one answered.

**Source (adapted):** [Nginx reverse proxy: error 413 on large file uploads](https://help.nextcloud.com/t/nginx-reverse-proxy-error-413-on-large-file-uploads/24335): uploads through the nginx proxies failed with 413 while the LAN worked; the poster had set `client_max_body_size` in only one place and fixed it by setting it in the `http` and the site's `server` context. The client-IP part follows forum threads such as [All visitors have same IP (my server IP)](https://ruby-forum.com/t/all-visitor-have-same-ip-my-server-ip/218759), where the answers were `proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;` and `X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;` plus making the backend trust them. Handbook: 43 §10.2.
